{{Quote|One way or another this ends today.|Kira Carsen|<ref name="Onslaught">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Onslaught]]''</ref>}}
A '''final confrontation''' against [[Tenebrae]] took place within the [[Mindscape|mind]] of [[Satele Shan]]<ref name="Echoes" /> in [[3626 BBY]].<ref name="Date" />

==Prelude==
Centuries prior to his apparent death during the [[Battle of Zakuul]], Tenebrae carved a [[Sith alchemy/Legends|Sith ritual]] into the flesh of his original body. The ritual was conditioned to unleash a [[Tenebrae's curse|dark plague]] if his body and spirit were destroyed and infect and invade the minds of anyone in the vicinity, feeding on their memories of the Emperor to recreate himself.<ref name="Echoes" />

[[File:Scourge_and_Kira_Carsen.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Lord Scourge and Kira Carsen]]
Shortly after the [[Battle of the Meridian Complex]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Scourge (Sith)|Scourge]] and the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kira Carsen]] revealed to the former [[Alliance Commander]] they had destroyed the original body of Tenebrae concurrently with the Commander's last confrontation with him. This act rendered them [[Coma/Legends|comatose]] for nearly a [[Time/Legends|year]], but they weren't affected beyond that as they had acted as vessels for Tenebrae's power in the past. They were rescued by Satele Shan and her [[Padawan/Legends|students]] who in turn were infected and began slowly merging into a [[Hive mind/Legends|hive mind]]. Carsen and Scourge then stole a cargo ship and quarantined the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] task force on board, sending them on a course through [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] away from any civilization.<ref name="Echoes" />

With Tenebrae threatening to return, the duo tested the Alliance Commander on [[Mek-Sha]] to make sure they were rid of Valkorion's hidden influences. Upon confirmation, they contacted the Commander (then the leader of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] [[Task Force Nova]]) to inform them of this threat.<ref name="Echoes" />

With Kira and Scourge having lost the ship, the Commander allowed them to send a search party composed of [[T7-O1]] and his [[Droid/Legends|droids]].<ref name="Echoes" />

==Mission==
===Kira Carsen's ship===
{{Quote|For the record... the ship was not this creepy when we left.|Kira Carsen, upon landing on her ship|<ref name="Onslaught" />}}
[[File:SatelesShipServants.png|thumb|left|250px|The Servants stand atop the bodies of slain Scions.]]
T7-01 managed to find the cargo ship and sent the coordinates to the trio, but was attacked by mysterious assailants and soon lost contact. The Commander, Scourge, and Carsen later arrived at the ship, immediately being attacked by unidentified individuals in an [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]] transport ship. This led Scourge to believe that the [[Servant]]s of the Sith Emperor had located their master through [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]. At a control panel, [[Servant Fifteen]] and [[Servant Twenty-two]] were repairing the systems of the ship and reporting to [[Servant Four]]. Lord Scourge, ruled by his new emotions, attacked and killed them in a blind rage, blowing their cover.<ref name="Echoes" />

After the skirmish, T7-01 came out of hiding and revealed that he had encountered a second vessel with no connection to the Servants. While T7 and Carsen disabled the ship's shields and weapons, the Commander and Scourge investigated and discovered that this vessel was of [[Zakuul]]. The Commander promptly ejected the shuttle into [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="Echoes" />

[[File:Revans_Ghost_on_Kiras_Ship.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Revan's Force Ghost appears before Scourge and the Commander.]]
Scourge and the Commander were then approached by the [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]] of [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], who guided them to the location of Satele Shan. Kira made contact with them and urged them to meet her in the medbay. In the medbay, they found the Servants placing the bodies of Satele and her students in a strange pattern, and encountered the [[Scions of Zakuul|Scion]] [[Minazar]]. Minazar, acting on a prophecy by the late [[Heskal]], came to the ship to resurrect Valkorion, declaring his intentions to preserve Valkorion's last vestige from the Servants' "corruption". Servant Four claimed that the Scions and the rest of Zakuul were merely puppets that never knew the true plan of the Emperor and that the Servants were his followers. Servant Four then killed Minazar and was joined by two more Servants, ready to face down the boarding party.<ref name="Echoes" />

Defeating the Servants, Kira rushed to Shan and her students. The Commander and Scourge then joined her in [[Meditation/Legends|meditation]] to enter Shan's mind.<ref name="Echoes" />

===Satele Shan's mind===
{{Quote|Everything you've done..."<br />"Everyone you've betrayed..."<br />"Everyone you've manipulated..."<br />"Everyone you've murdered..."<br />"The Force seeks balance. Always.|Satele, Senya, Kira, Meetra, and Revan to Tenebrae just before his death|<ref name="Onslaught" />}}
[[File:Valkorions_family.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Valkorion's family arrives for the final stand against the tyrant.]]
Having successfully entered Shan's mind, the Commander and Kira Carsen encountered Valkorion, who did not appear to recognize them. Two other figures then emerged, representing Vitiate and Tenebrae, the latter of whom condemned Valkorion for becoming distracted by "mortal concerns". Tenebrae vowed to not make the same mistake. The trinity then separated the Commander from their allies, but they were soon joined by Revan, who assisted the Commander in reaching the center of the mindscape. Confronting the trinity once more, the Commander and Revan was taunted by Tenebrae, who boasted of his alleged invincibility. Suddenly, [[Meetra Surik]] appeared, declaring that everything, including Tenebrae, inevitably dies. Tenebrae reminded that she failed to strike him down in the past. Scourge also appeared, stating that while he chose to save him then, he would not save him now. Tenebrae then lashed out to again separate the Commander from their comrades. The Commander was met by the spirit of [[Darth Marr]], who explained that Tenebrae underestimates Satele's resilience, while only gleaming the memories and impressions that Satele and her students have of his original self, but lacks any of the wisdom. He advised the Commander not to share in his arrogance, as while Tenebrae is more vulnerable than he believed, he was still the most dangerous being in the galaxy, and urged them to avenge him and everyone else who had been killed by the Emperor. The Commander was also joined by [[Senya Tirall]], [[Arcann]], [[Thexan]], and [[Vaylin]] who also were trying to stop Valkorion from returning.<ref name="Echoes" />

The Commander reached the center of the mindscape, a memory of the [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]. Within, Tenebrae's trinity encircled Satele Shan and arrogantly declared victory over her. Satele then awoke and mocked Tenebrae for his arrogance, revealing she had exploited his ego, knowing he would've extended himself in trying to dominate her and her students instead of just one, buying enough time for the Commander to arrive. In the ensuing battle, the combined forces of the living and dead who were wronged by the Emperor fought the trinity one by one, withstanding his immense power. Unwilling to accept defeat, Tenebrae's trinity combined their powers, almost bringing their combined foes to their knees, when suddenly the Commander and their allies began to rise, radiating with golden light as the spirits of the countless people the Emperor had killed, manipulated and betrayed appeared. Revan then proclaimed that the Force will always seek balance. The Emperor's power soon turned back on the trinity, as Vitiate, Valkorion, and Tenebrae turned to stone and crumbled to dust in a similar fashion to the devastations of [[Nathema]] and [[Ziost/Legends|Ziost]]. Even in his final moments, Tenebrae tried to deny the reality of his situation, proclaiming he commanded the Force, but the Commander retorted that in the end, he was nothing.<ref name="Echoes" />

==Aftermath==
Satele would then take the Commander to an illusion of a forest campfire as an impromptu victory party, where she declared that the Sith Emperor was well and truly dead. She then informed the Commander that Carsen and Scourge were taking her students back to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], while Arcann and Senya were returning to Odessen, and expressed hope they would find peace at last. As for Darth Marr, Meetra Surik and Revan, she believed they had become one with the Force at last. Before sending the Commander back to reality, she proclaimed the galaxy finally free of Tenebrae's dark influence and now a new future can begin.<ref name="Echoes" />

The Commander would later wake up on the shuttle with Lana Beniko, who informed her superior that Carsen and Scourge were the first to wake up from ritual and brought the Commander's unconscious body to her. With the Commander having been unconscious for an hour, Beniko inquired what happened. The Commander informed her of their conversation with Satele, and promised to explain in detail, before ordering Beniko to plot a new hyperspace course.<ref name="Echoes" />

Satele Shan would return to Coruscant, where she was approached by former Jedi Knight, [[Aryn Leneer]].<ref name="Echoes" />

==Behind the scenes==
If the player is either a Jedi Knight or Sith Warrior at the start of the mission, they would express familiarity with the Servants.<ref name="Echoes" />

If [[Theron Shan]] was spared in '''The Nathema Conspiracy''' flashpoint, the player can either allow or forbid him from joining the mission. If the latter is chosen, Theron would defy orders and follow in a Zakuul shuttle, helping provide covering fire for the Commander's shuttle to dock with Carsen's ship.<ref name="Nathema">{{TORcite|exp=kotet|type=general|The Nathema Conspiracy|Nathema}}</ref> <ref name="Echoes" />

After encountering Revan's ghost on the bridge, Scourge will tell the Jedi Knight that after their fatal encounter with Revan on Yavin 4, he avoided mentioning his former ally as the source of his information because he wasn't sure Carsen would trust him. For all other player classes, Scourge will simply say that because Carsen fought the Revanites on Yavin 4, he wasn't sure she would trust him.<ref name="Echoes" />

The player has three dialogues choices with Servant Four:
*If player says the Sith were a means to an end, Servant Four fiercely rejects those words as lies.<ref name="Echoes" />
*If the player agreed with the Sith, saying the Zakuulans never knew the true nature of their Immortal Emperor, Minazar would indignantly label the player as ignorant, claiming the Scions' visions pierced all truths. Servant Four retorted that Valkorion showed the Scions only what he allowed while exploiting their minds and body as fuel for his immortality.<ref name="Echoes" />
*If the player says both the Sith and Scions were deceived by an uncaring master, Servant Four proclaimed it his right as a god.<ref name="Echoes" />

If [[Arcann]] and [[Senya Tirall]] survived the events of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Eternal Throne|Knights of the Eternal Throne]]'' expansion, they would both make an emotional plea, asserting that Valkorion manipulated the Servants as surely as he did his own family.<ref name="Echoes" />

Regardless, Servant Four would execute Minazar regardless.<ref name="Echoes" />

Prior to the final confrontation, Tenebrae will have different comments on the player's class:
*For the '''Sith Warrior''' or the '''Sith Inquisitor''', he proclaimed himself master of all Sith and dismisses the idea any can challenge his power.<ref name="Echoes" />
*For the '''Jedi Knight''' or the '''Jedi Consular''', he refuses to be defeated by a "mere Jedi.<ref name="Echoes" />
*For the '''Republic Trooper''', he arrogantly asks how a "mere soldier" could hope to challenge him.<ref name="Echoes" />
*For the '''Bounty Hunter''', he dismisses the idea he could be defeated by an "ignorant hired gun".<ref name="Echoes" />
*For the '''Smuggler''', he calls them an " insignificant vagabond".<ref name="Echoes" />
*For the '''Imperial Agent''', he calls them an "ignorant tool of an empire I created!"<ref name="Echoes" />

The player can respond with a corresponding class dialogue:
*The '''Sith Warrior''' can say, "You named me your Wrath. Here, now... I can think of no better name."<ref name="Echoes" />
*The '''Sith Inquisitor''' can say, "Everyone who has stood in my way - who has challenged or threatened me - has been destroyed. Including you."<ref name="Echoes" />
*The '''Republic Trooper''' can say, "I'll win the same way I always do: as part of a team."<ref name="Echoes" />
*The '''Smuggler''' can say, "Again. What you mean to say, is that you won't be killed by an "insignificant vagabond... again."<ref name="Echoes" />
*The '''Jedi Knight''' or '''Jedi Consular''' can say, "You think your power is infinite. Only the Force is infinite. I am one with the Force... and the Force is with me."<ref name="Echoes" />
*The '''Imperial Agent''' can say, "You truly think it's impossible - that what makes it possible."<ref name="Echoes" />
*The '''Bounty Hunter''' can say, "Nobody hired me this time. I'm taking you down for free."<ref name="Echoes" />

After the battle, the player and Satele appear in the illusion of a campfire. Depending on whether or not Theron Shan survived the events of the previous expansion, Satele will either thank the player for giving her son a home she never could or bluntly note Theron's death. If the player had killed Theron, they can choose the dark side option and attempt to kill her, only for Satele, who acknowledges the player very well could, to reveal that she's not physically present. Depending on the player's light or dark side alignment, Satele can either express hope for the future free of Tenebrae or forewarn the player not to follow his path, reminding that for all his power, the weight of his wrongdoing was his downfall.<ref name="Echoes" />
